answer: In an agent economy coordinating mesa surveys, quill shipments, and ridge inspections, each identity must lock 100 tokens in escrow for 30 days to hold one active job slot. Splitting into more identities creates no free capacity: an attacker seeking 1,000 simultaneous slots must immobilize 100,000 tokens for the full month. The bond makes a swarm expensive through capital lockup, even though creating names is free.
